Campaign brief: You can have an agent answering handbook questions inside Slack, grounded in your own documents, without building or owning the retrieval layer that makes it work.
events.reader:
Selected audience: Ops or IT generalist standing up an internal Slack answer-bot over company docs.
Situation context (grounded; check applicability): This is an ops/IT-adjacent person at a company where policies and handbooks are written up in Notion or similar docs and employees communicate primarily in Slack; when someone can't find an answer, they ping this person (or the team channel) directly, and this person has been asked to build or is considering building an automated Slack responder that draws on the Handbook, Docs, and Issue Trackers.
events.reader_segment: Ops or IT generalist standing up an internal Slack answer-bot over company docs
events.promise: You can have an agent answering handbook questions inside Slack, grounded in your own documents, without building or owning the retrieval layer that makes it work.
events.arc: Single email, so the whole arc happens inside it: from "an internal answer-bot is a build somebody here would have to own" to "it is a configuration over documents I already have, and I can test it against last week's questions before anyone else sees it." The email opens on the reader's recurring problem, names what people do today, states plainly what is now available and how it is put together, and ends on a first test that is small enough to run alone.

emails.job: Get the reader to create a free account and stand up one agent over one set of handbook documents connected to Slack — a first test they can run alone, not a rollout they have to sell internally.
emails.single_idea: orqAgent is available now: point an agent at your own handbook documents, connect it to Slack, and the repeat policy questions get answered in the channel — without you standing up or maintaining the retrieval layer underneath it.
emails.objection: Nobody here owns internal tooling — if I stand this up, who keeps it running afterwards?
must_not_say: No plan prices, credit counts, execution limits or run limits. The published pricing tables contradict each other across pages, and quoting a number invites the reader to catch it. The ask is a free sign-up, not a priced comparison.
No SOC 2, certification or compliance claims of any kind — SOC 2 is only in progress and this reader is not running an IT review yet.
No guardrail claims (PII masking, content filtering, prompt injection detection) — capability state is unknown for this campaign.

Do not claim the Google Docs import, the other channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Email Inbox, webhooks), Enterprise features, SSO/SAML, SLA or uptime figures. Notion and Slack are the only integrations this email may name.

Do not name or compare against Slack's own AI, Dust, Glean, n8n-as-a-product or any per-seat workspace assistant, and do not argue breadth, quality, speed, control, security or track record against the field. Describe the approach, never a named rival.
No customer names, logos, user counts, testimonials or 'teams like yours' — none exist in the material and none may be implied.

Do not characterise retrieval quality, accuracy, or claim semantic or embedding search. State that relevant context is retrieved automatically and invite the reader to test it on their own documents; do not promise it answers every question or answers them correctly.
No deflection percentages, hours saved, ticket reductions or any quantified outcome.
Do not claim it replaces documentation search, a knowledge base, a helpdesk, a backend or anyone's job — it answers questions in a channel.
No API, curl, JSON schema, endpoint or key-handling detail. This reader works from the console; a code block loses them.

Do not state as fact that this reader already built a bot, abandoned one, lost weeks to maintenance, or has no tooling owner. Any build scenario stays conditional — 'if you have been asked to stand one up'.
Do not claim a full company-wide rollout time, or extend the documented setup speed into a claim about being live for everyone in minutes.
No hype vocabulary: no 'revolutionary', 'game-changing', 'cutting-edge', 'leverage', 'synergy', 'solution'. No exclamation marks.
Do not promise voice or telephony support unless a current licensed source explicitly establishes it.
Do not claim that the agent layer replaces a company's complete backend, product UI, billing, or operational workflow without direct evidence.
Compliance and certification claims are unavailable unless the Evidence Ledger explicitly licenses them.
Do not claim Knowledge base / RAG context; its capability state is unknown.
Do not claim Agent guardrails; its capability state is unknown.
Do not claim Reusable per-client agent configuration; its capability state is unknown.
Do not claim Voice and telephony runtime; its capability state is unsupported.
Do not claim Full SaaS backend replacement; its capability state is unsupported.
Do not claim HIPAA compliance; its capability state is unknown.
Do not claim Deep domain-specific operational integrations; its capability state is unknown.

Retrieval is keyword scoring over roughly 500-token chunks (E56, E57) rather than semantic search, and the free tier caps the knowledge base at five documents (E120), so a question worded unlike the handbook or spread across a large page.
emails.felt_need: The same policy and handbook questions get asked repeatedly in Slack, and the answers are buried in documentation that is difficult to navigate.
emails.status_quo: Team members search Notion by trying random keywords or guessing document titles rather than getting a direct answer.
emails.why_it_fails: Keyword-guessing across a few hundred pages takes several searches before the answer surfaces, and it often turns up three sections deep in a page nobody expected. The low-code wiring route is openly described by the people using it as a jetpack rather than a long-haul aircraft — not suited to high-scale, latency-sensitive use or to anything needing real observability — which leaves the person who built it as the one who keeps it flying.
emails.mechanism: The two pieces you would otherwise assemble are configuration here, not a build. Documents are uploaded — or Notion pages and databases synced over OAuth — and the most relevant context is retrieved for each question automatically, with no vector database to manage. Slack is an OAuth install, after which the bot replies to mentions and channel messages in the place the questions already arrive.

events.body:
Someone asks in the channel where the expense policy sits. The answer is in the handbook — three sections deep in a page nobody would think to open.

So it gets found the long way: a few keyword guesses against Notion, a guess at the document title, then a copy-paste back into Slack.

orqAgent is available now. It is a no-code platform for building AI agents, and the shape it takes here is narrow: one agent, one set of handbook documents, one channel.

Upload the documents, or sync Notion pages and databases over OAuth. The agent retrieves the most relevant context for each question automatically — there is no vector database to stand up or manage.

Slack is an OAuth install. After that, the bot replies to mentions and channel messages, in the place the questions already arrive. No infrastructure to manage, and the setup happens in the console.

Point one agent at one set of handbook documents and ask it the questions you answered by hand last week. The first agent takes **under two minutes**, no credit card.
